questions.question_text: Who among the following was the first Surveyor General of India, responsible for preparing the first detailed map of the Vijayanagara site at Hampi?
According to the Ain-i-Akbari, which category of land was continuously cultivated and never left fallow?
In the context of the Mughal agrarian system, what did the term 'Milkiyat' refer to?
options: B) Personal land owned by the zamindars
C) Land granted to religious institutions
questions.answer: B) Personal land owned by the zamindars

questions.question_text: Which prominent leader argued strongly against separate electorates in the Constituent Assembly, stating it was a 'poison that has entered the body politic of our country'?
The famous 'Hazara Rama Temple', meant to be used only by the king and his family, was located in which part of Vijayanagara?
In the Mughal revenue system, the amount of revenue assessed was known as 'Jama'. What was the amount actually collected called?
The 'Sunset Law' was a crucial and strict component of which colonial revenue system?
Who was the British Governor-General during the outbreak of the Revolt of 1857?
The historic Dandi March, initiating the Civil Disobedience Movement, began from which location?
Explain the significance of the Kamalapuram tank and the Hiriya canal in the water management system of the Vijayanagara Empire. [35-45 words]
questions.answer: The Kamalapuram tank captured rainwater to irrigate local agricultural fields and supplied water to the Royal Centre through a complex channel network. The Hiriya canal, drawing water from a Tungabhadra dam, specifically irrigated the sacred center and urban core, demonstrating advanced hydrological engineering.

questions.question_text: Describe the core responsibilities and socio-economic power of the Zamindars in the Mughal agrarian framework. [35-45 words]
questions.answer: Mughal Zamindars were landed aristocrats who did not directly participate in agricultural production but collected land revenue on behalf of the state. They enjoyed widespread social dominance, commanded personal military contingents, and held hereditary rights (Milkiyat) over vast landholdings and fortresses.

questions.question_text: Why did many Zamindars default on the payment of land revenue during the initial decades of the Permanent Settlement in Bengal? [35-45 words]
questions.answer: Zamindars defaulted because the initial revenue demands were fixed exorbitantly high. Furthermore, agricultural prices were depressed, making it difficult for ryots to pay rent. The stringent 'Sunset Law' heavily penalized delays, leading to the immediate auction of estates when payments were missed.

questions.question_text: Analyze how the introduction of the Subsidiary Alliance by Lord Wellesley systematically eroded the sovereignty of Indian native states. [35-45 words]
questions.answer: The Subsidiary Alliance forced native rulers to disband their independent armies, host a permanent British garrison, and pay for its maintenance. It also prohibited them from forming alliances or declaring war without British permission, effectively reducing sovereign kings to powerless, dependent figureheads.

questions.question_text: Briefly outline the historical significance of the Salt March (Dandi March) in expanding the mass base of the Indian National Movement. [35-45 words]
questions.answer: The Salt March transformed the national struggle into a genuine mass movement by mobilizing peasants, workers, and notably women across India against an unjust tax on a basic necessity. It drew massive global media attention, exposing the moral bankruptcy of British colonial rule.

questions.question_text: Why did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar strongly advocate for constitutional safeguards and political reservations for the Depressed Classes in the Constituent Assembly? [35-45 words]
questions.answer: Ambedkar argued that the Depressed Classes suffered not just economic backwardness, but systemic social isolation and stigma. He insisted that without explicit constitutional reservations in legislatures and government jobs, mere political independence would not dismantle untouchability or ensure their true democratic representation.

sections.section_name: Section C - Long-Form Narrative & Analytical Essays

questions.question_text: Deconstruct the architectural layout and political symbolism of the 'Royal Centre' in Vijayanagara. Highlight the specific functions of the Mahanavami Dibba and the Lotus Mahal in projecting imperial authority. [100-120 words]
questions.answer: The Royal Centre of Vijayanagara, situated in the southwestern part of the settlement, housed over sixty temples and thirty grand palatial complexes, constructed meticulously with stone and rubble masonry. It was designed to project absolute imperial authority. The Mahanavami Dibba, a towering two-tiered platform, was the focal point of the spectacular ten-day Mahanavami festival. Here, the Raya displayed his suzerainty by receiving tributes from Nayakas, conducting state rituals, and reviewing grand military processions. The Lotus Mahal, named for its distinctive arches, functioned as an elite council chamber where the king met his chief advisers. Together, these monumental structures intertwined religious patronage with immense political theater, reinforcing the Raya's image as the supreme divine representative on earth.

questions.question_text: Examine the visions of unity forged among the rebels during the Revolt of 1857. How did they attempt to establish alternative structures of authority after collapsing the British administration? [100-120 words]
questions.answer: During the Revolt of 1857, the rebels forged a remarkable vision of unity that transcended religious boundaries. Rebel proclamations explicitly appealed to both Hindus and Muslims, emphasizing a shared cultural heritage and mutual loss under oppressive British policies. Symbols like the restoration of Bahadur Shah Zafar highlighted a collective desire to return to the pre-colonial socio-political order. Once British authority collapsed, rebel leaders in centers like Delhi, Lucknow, and Kanpur attempted to establish alternative administrative structures. They formed councils, appointed officials to collect land revenue, and set up military commands to fund and direct the war effort. Though these structures were often fragile and localized, they reflected a sophisticated attempt to completely dismantle colonial rule and restore sovereign, indigenous governance.

questions.question_text: Analyze how Mahatma Gandhi successfully transformed the Indian National Movement from an elite middle-class agitation into a genuinely mass-based struggle between 1915 and 1922. [100-120 words]
questions.answer: Between 1915 and 1922, Mahatma Gandhi revolutionized the Indian National Movement by shifting its base from elite professionals to the rural masses. He achieved this by adopting the lifestyle, dress, and language of ordinary peasants, notably wearing a simple dhoti and promoting Hindustani. His early local interventions in Champaran, Kheda, and Ahmedabad proved the efficacy of Satyagraha (non-violent resistance) to address grassroots economic grievances. By linking the Khilafat issue with the Non-Cooperation Movement, he successfully unified Hindus and Muslims against colonial rule. Gandhi also restructured the Congress party, creating provincial committees based on linguistic zones, which decentralized leadership. By promoting Charkha (spinning wheel) and Swadeshi, he economically empowered the masses, forging a unified, national anti-imperialist consciousness.

questions.question_text: Read the historical extract regarding Mughal revenue: 'The Amil-guzar should ascertain the exact state of the crops... He should collect the revenue in cash, though in some cases payment in kind may be accepted. The Jama is the amount assessed, and the Hasil is the amount actually collected.' Analyze the structural flexibility in the Mughal revenue administration as evident in this passage. [45-55 words]
questions.answer: The passage reveals a highly structured yet pragmatic Mughal revenue system. While cash payments were preferred to stabilize state treasuries, the administration demonstrated flexibility by accepting payments in kind based on regional crop realities. The clear distinction between Jama (assessed) and Hasil (collected) indicates sophisticated accounting mechanisms to track administrative efficiency and agrarian distress.

questions.question_text: Read the Fifth Report extract: 'When the estates of the defaulting Zamindar of Burdwan were auctioned, a large number of the purchasers turned out to be servants and agents of the Raja himself. Thus, the lands remained in his control, and the Company lost its arrears.' Evaluate the subversive tactics used by traditional Zamindars to bypass the Permanent Settlement's strict auction laws. [45-55 words]
questions.answer: The extract exposes how powerful Zamindars subverted the draconian 'Sunset Law' through fictitious sales. By deploying benami purchasers—their own servants and agents—to outbid others at auctions, they refused to pay the purchase money later. This forced repeated, failed auctions, ultimately allowing the original Zamindar to retain his ancestral estate at vastly reduced revenue demands.

questions.question_text: Read the Constituent Assembly debate excerpt by Somnath Lahiri: 'We must not frame our Constitution under the dark shadow of British imperialism... The Interim Government is merely a British creation.' Analyze Lahiri’s critique and explain the pressure it put on the Assembly regarding true democratic sovereignty. [45-55 words]
questions.answer: Somnath Lahiri’s critique highlights the deep anxiety among radical members that the Constituent Assembly, born out of the Cabinet Mission Plan, was still chained to British imperial machinations. He pressured the Assembly to assert absolute sovereign independence, urging members to politically liberate the constitution-making process from colonial oversight and deeply rooted imperial administrative frameworks.

sections.section_name: Section E - Hands-on Location & Map Work

questions.question_text: On an outline political map of India, identify and label the precise locations of five major historical centers central to the Themes in Indian History curriculum, marked as follows: 'Site A' (The capital city of the Vijayanagara Empire), 'Site B' (The Mughal capital founded by Akbar), 'Site C' (The cantonment where the Revolt of 1857 began), 'Site D' (The site of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre), and 'Site E' (The location of Gandhi's first Satyagraha for indigo farmers). [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The structural map coordinates align precisely with these historical centers: Site A marks Hampi (Karnataka), the imperial nucleus of Vijayanagara. Site B identifies Fatehpur Sikri (Uttar Pradesh), the grand architectural capital built by Akbar. Site C points to Meerut (Uttar Pradesh), the spark of 1857. Site D locates Amritsar (Punjab), and Site E marks Champaran (Bihar).
